Subject: Clarifying pricing metrics — tokens vs characters vs requests

Hi Sam — great to chat earlier. Quick recap + a couple of clarifying questions so we size things correctly on our side and can put together an accurate cost estimate: 

1) Traffic profile you mentioned: ~12M API calls/month across the assistant and summarization endpoints, with average prompt length ~350 characters and average response ~1,100 characters. Is that per-call on average or skewed by a subset of long reports?
2) You asked about our billed unit — we bill per token (1 token ≈ 4 characters for English on average), not per request or per character. So rough conversion: 1M tokens ≈ 4M characters.
3) Caching: prompt caching helps reduce billed tokens only if you use prefix caching for repeated prompts and we return cached responses without regenerating. If you cache on your side (e.g., de-duplicate identical prompts before calling), that reduces requests but we only bill for tokens processed by Redwood.

Two asks: can you share a small sample of 1,000 recent prompts (anonymized) so our pricing model can compute tokens distribution? I attached a template (sample-prompt-sets.txt) and a simple pricing model workbook (redwood_pricing-model.xlsx) that shows unit economics at different token volumes and target $/1M token buckets.

Target next steps: if you can send the sample prompts and confirm whether you will use client-side dedupe or want Redwood to enable prefix caching, we’ll run the numbers and propose a 3-tier pricing sketch (hosted + reserved commit options).

Thanks,

Good question, Sam — short answer: we bill for tokens processed by Redwood (input tokens + output tokens). So if you stop sending redundant requests upstream (de-dup at gateway) you save both request count and billed tokens. But if you aggregate or batch multiple user messages into a single prompt, you may actually increase tokens per request — billed tokens reflect actual model I/O. 

A few specific notes to make decisions easier: 
- Tokens vs characters: our billing is token-based. Use the conversion in the workbook (~4 chars ≈ 1 token) as a rule of thumb; we'll run exact tokenization on your samples. 
- Requests vs tokens: requests matter for concurrency/latency (we size instances by RPS/throughput) but cost is driven by tokens. So both are relevant for ops and pricing (we might recommend a commit that considers peak QPS).
- Prompt caching vs billed tokens: Redwood's prefix caching returns cached responses without re-running the model only for identical prompt prefixes we detect within your configured window. Those cached hits do not incur model token compute (so not billed as tokens), though we may bill a small metadata request cost if you use advanced cache policies — I'll flag that in the model.

I'll have Rishi run your sample through our tokenizer and send back a cost projection with three target $/1M token bands: $600/1M, $350/1M, $175/1M (hosted -> committed -> private/dedicated). Marcus will put together recommended commit sizes based on your 12M-call profile and the expected token breakdown.

Marissa

On a side note — for long reports we sometimes recommend streaming + chunking to keep latency predictable and avoid repeated full-document regenerations.

Hi Sam / Marissa — I ran the anonymized 1k prompt sample through our tokenizer this morning (thanks for sending it over, Sam). High-level takeaways: 

- Median tokens per request: 180 
- 75th percentile: 560 tokens (driven by summary responses)
- 95th percentile: 3,800 tokens (long report generation)

Using your 12M calls/month mix and assuming client-side dedupe reduces identical prompts by ~20%, our model shows approximate billed tokens/month: ~1.9B tokens. Attached is the pricing sketch in the workbook with the three tiers Marissa mentioned: 

- Hosted (no commit): $600 / 1M tokens → est $1,140,000/month
- Committed Reserved (6-12mo): $350 / 1M tokens → est $665,000/month (with sliding discounts at higher commits)
- Dedicated Private (multi-year, custom): $175 / 1M tokens → est $332,500/month (requires infra commitments)

Notes: these numbers assume prefix caching yields ~12% cache-hit rate on the assistant prompts; increasing caching to 25% reduces billed tokens by ~10–12% overall. I'll send a final table with sensitivity to cache-hit and dedupe rates.

Next step: Marcus — can you draft a recommended commit band (3 options: conservative / target / aggressive) and I’ll attach the sensitivity tables so Acme can pick a target $/1M token and corresponding commit? Sam — if you prefer, we can show equivalent requests-per-second sizing for each band.
